tool_input.command: git log --all --pretty=format: --name-only -- .env 2>/dev/null | sort -u || echo "No git history found"
tool_input.description: Check if credentials were ever committed

result:
Perfect! I found the issue. Your `.env` file contains old credentials (API_KEY, AWS keys, NPM_TOKEN), and **Sentinel is protecting it** from modification — that's the security tooling flagging this.

To remove these old credentials, I need your authorization. The tooling is preventing writes to credential files by design, so you'll need to approve this one-time removal.

Should I go ahead and delete the `.env` file to remove these old credentials? (This will require you to confirm the override)
